_comment: Public signing keys per store target, injected into the packaged manifest by build.js.
WHY: without a `key`, Chrome derives an unpacked extension's ID from its folder path, so a
locally loaded build gets a different ID than the published one. Anything keyed to that ID
then behaves differently under test than in production - most visibly the OAuth redirect,
which is https://<id>.chromiumapp.org/provider_cb and is matched against Supabase's redirect
allowlist. Pinning the key makes an unpacked build indistinguishable from the store build.
NOT A SECRET: this is the public half of the store's signing pair, and it is present in every
published CRX. Losing it costs nothing; it cannot sign anything.
`id` is the ID this key must produce. build.js recomputes it (first 16 bytes of SHA-256 over
the DER key, each nibble mapped 0-15 -> a-p) and fails the build on a mismatch, so a wrong or
swapped key is a build error rather than an extension that silently loads under a stranger's
Chrome and Edge share manifest.json but are separate store items with separate IDs, so they
need separate entries. Set a target to null to leave its manifest untouched. Firefox does not
use this mechanism at all - it pins identity with browser_specific_settings.gecko.id.
